title: Legacy of the Departed
next_chapter_hook: The moment Mo Xiansheng's words fell, the third page of the Tianji Record suddenly glowed with a faint light, and an ancient script that had never appeared before slowly emerged—that was the core secret concerning the 'Heavenly Fate Lock Key'.

text.content: The sound of the door closing echoed in the silent stone chamber. Chen Ji stood motionless, fingers unconsciously rubbing the Tianji Record at his waist. Those words were like a fine needle, precisely pricking the corner he least wanted to touch—his master's choice back then. Trust. Hesneered一声，将那两个字在心底碾碎。 The mysterious helper knew too much, enough to send a chill down his spine.

He didn't immediately return to his meditation chamber, standing for a long while in the shadows at the end of the corridor. Moonlight filtered through the window lattice, stretching his shadow long and distorted. The night at Tianqing Sect was always exceptionally quiet, so quiet that one could hear one's own heartbeat. He closed his eyes, letting that name surge through his mind—Chen Xuan. His father, also the previous master of the Tianji Record. The truth of this stirred waves in his heart far more violent than the composed facade suggested.

dialogue.content: Young Master, your heart is troubled.

text.content: Mo Xiansheng's voice echoed from within the Tianji Record, aged and weary. Chen Ji opened his eyes, the turmoil within them suppressed, replaced by his customary composure and calculation. 'Troubled?' His voice carried no inflection. 'I was merely contemplating who that person could be.' He paused. 'And... how many more things have you been hiding from me.' The cover of the Tianji Record grew slightly warm, as if responding to his accusation.

Upon returning to his meditation chamber, Chen Ji did not immediately rest. He retrieved the tattered map obtained from the ancient ruins from his chest, spreading it across the candlelit table. This was one of his key pieces for maneuvering the world—the routes to three secret realms, crucial to his fundamental ability to ride the chaos and dominate. Yet tonight, for the first time, he examined it with different eyes. Had his master seen this map too? He suppressed the thought, beginning to carefully inspect every detail that might have been overlooked.

The candlelight danced, casting flickering shadows across the map's surface. Chen Ji's gaze was as sharp as a hawk's, sweeping from the eastern sea regions to the western frontier deserts, searching every inch. When his finger traced a marking on the northern frozen lands, his movement abruptly halted. Beside the position he had marked as a 'deadly ground', there was a faint ink trace—if not for the candlelight恰好以某个角度照射，绝不可能被发现。

Chen Ji held his breath, drawing the map closer to the flame. Those ink marks were not ordinary annotations, but an extremely concealed talisman—bearing a striking resemblance to the seal pattern on his Tianji Record's cover. His pupils contracted sharply, and a realization struck him like lightning: this was a marker left by his master. He took a deep breath, gently placing his fingertip on the talisman,whispered念动咒语。 Instantly, the Tianji Record flew out on its own, hovering above the map!

The pages of the Tianji Record fluttered without wind, turning to a page that had never appeared before—the seventh page. Where there should have been blank space, a faint blue light now shimmered, with a blurry figure gradually forming within the glow. Chen Ji stared intently at that silhouette, his heart pounding like a war drum. It was a middle-aged man in blue robes, his features bearing a seventy percent resemblance to Chen Ji's own, yet with a gentle, warm smile that Chen Ji had never possessed. His father, whom he had never seen—Chen Xuan.

Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul trembled violently. Chen Ji clearly felt the emotional fluctuations transmitted by the Tianji Record—that was shock, disbelief, and an almost agonizing complexity. 'How could this be...' Mo Xiansheng's voice trembled severely, 'How could he leave a mark here? Young Master, your father... he never mentioned the existence of this map to me!' Chen Ji said nothing, merely carving every detail of that figure into his mind.

dialogue.content: There are many things he didn't mention. Mo Xiansheng, I ask you—how did my father die?

text.content: This question was like a blade, cutting through thegrave气氛 of the meditation chamber. Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul fell into an extended silence, so prolonged that Chen Ji initially believed he would not answer. 'In those days...' Mo Xiansheng's voice was艰涩, 'The moment the Tianji Record selected its successor was already fated.' He paused. 'Every master of the Tianji Record becomes a pawn of Heavenly Dao. The young master's father did not die by another's hand—he was erased by the Will of Heaven.'

The Will of Heaven. Chen Ji碾过舌尖的这四个字，icy的触感从脊椎蔓延至四肢。 He had long suspected this—the Tianji Record's abilities were too逆天, yet the cost was merely aHeavenly Fate Value, which was inherently unreasonable. Now everything made sense. He was not a blessed favorite, but a chosen sacrifice. Every ounce of ability to foresee the future was a debt owed to that ultimate existence.

dialogue.content: But that wasn't everything. Mo Xiansheng's voice continued,带着一种破釜沉舟的determined, 'Young Master, do you know... when your father chose to inherit the Tianji Record, it was to protect someone?'

choice.prompt: The deep meaning in Mo Xiansheng's words left Chen Ji in a momentary silence. He隐约猜到了答案，却不敢确认。

choices.description: Directly confronting Mo Xiansheng, demanding the complete truth—he was fed up with being kept in the dark.
choices.risk_hint: Mo Xiansheng may have held something back

text.content: Chen Ji's voicesuddenlycold and stern: 'Who?' The two words landed with unwavering force,不容回避。 The pages of the Tianji Record剧烈翻动, as Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul seemed to endure some kind of torment. After a long, agonizing silence, he finally spoke: 'Your sister... Chen Nian.' This name struck like a heavy hammer, leaving Chen Ji's vision swimming.

dialogue.content: Chen Nian possessed aHeavenly Fate Lock Key constitution, which would interfere with the perception of all prophetic-type treasures. The moment your father inherited the Tianji Record, he察觉到 her anomaly—she was the only variable against the Will of Heaven. The Holy Sect taking her was not coincidental, but rather...

choices.description: He suppressed the surging emotions in his heart, waiting patiently for Mo Xiansheng to explain the full story—he knew some things could not be rushed.

text.content: Chen Ji said nothing, only slowly releasing his clenched fists. Mo Xiansheng seemed to sense his restraint, sighing: "Young master is more... patient than your father was." The blue light of the remnant soul dimmed slightly. "Your sister's physique is the true reason the Holy Sect targeted her. Your father, as the master of the Tianji Record, used himself as bait to draw away all the pursuers, thus preserving her life."

dialogue.content: But what your father didn't anticipate was that Heavenly Fate had long since set in motion an even deeper game. It had the Holy Sect take Chen Nian, not to kill her—but to nurture her into... a key.

choices.memory_label: 墨先生首次完整透露往事

choices.text: Inquiring about the Mysterious Helper's Identity
choices.description: The mysterious benefactor's identity is equally suspicious—how does he know about your master's choices from back then?

text.content: A sharp light flickered in Chen Ji's eyes: "That benefactor... do you know him?" Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul shuddered violently, as if struck by some painful point. "That person..." His voice was hoarse, "I cannot be certain. But there was a trace of aura on him, extremely similar to your father..." Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply, and a turbulent wave surged in his heart.

dialogue.content: It's also possible... it was a contingency left by your father. He fell too suddenly that year, perhaps with arrangements we knew nothing about. Mo Xiansheng's tone turned grave. "Regardless, this person knows far too much—he is by no means trustworthy. Young master must be careful."

text.content: Key. Chen Ji rolled the word across his tongue, tasting a heavy bitterness. He thought of Chen Nian's disappearance when he was still a naive child, the mysterious figures who always appeared at the Mid-Yuan Festival lantern fairs over the years, and the "coincidences" he had always believed in—every time he fell into a desperate situation, invisible hands would be at work behind the scenes. He thought he had seen through fate, not knowing he was merely a single piece on a much larger chessboard.

The candle flame flickered again, and the glow of the rune on the map gradually dimmed. However, in the instant before the figure was about to vanish, Chen Ji saw clearly what his father held in his hand—a Jade Pendant, exactly identical to the one he had worn close to his body since childhood, though he had never investigated its origin. His breath hastened, and a long-buried memory broke through the earth: the words his mother had pressed into his palm as she lay dying—"This is left for you by your father. He said... when you grow up, you will understand."

Chen Ji tore open his robe abruptly, taking out the Jade Pendant he had worn for twenty years. The jade was warm and smooth, its color dull and dark, appearing unremarkable at first glance. Yet now, he brought the Jade Pendant close to the rune on the map—in that instant, a幽蓝的光芒从玉佩中迸发而出，与地图上的符文遥相呼应，一道苍老而warm的声音在他脑海中响起："机儿，若你看到这段话，说明为父已经不在了……"

choice.prompt: His father's voice crossed the boundary of life and death, and Chen Ji felt his heart gripped tight by an invisible hand.

choices.description: Holding breath and focusing, carving every word into the depths of his heart—this was his father's final testament left to him.

text.content: That voice continued, each word carrying infinite exhaustion and longing: "The Tianji Record chose you, not by coincidence. Your bloodline carries the destiny of a prophet, but more importantly—your sister Chen Nian is the tool Heavenly Fate uses to restart the world. I passed the Tianji Record to you, hoping you would..." The voice cut off abruptly, as if severed by some force.

Chen Ji clenched the Jade Pendant tightly, his knuckles white. "Want me to do what?" he demanded in a low voice, his voice echoing in the empty quiet chamber, but there was no response. The light of the Jade Pendant was completely extinguished, and the runes on the map returned to silence. Mo Xiansheng's voice sounded, carrying undisguised shock: "This is... Memory Seal. Your father sealed the most crucial information within this Jade Pendant!"

choices.description: Suppress emotions with force, mobilize all strategies to analyze the information at hand—he cannot let feelings influence his judgment.

text.content: Chen Ji closed his eyes, forcibly pressing the surging emotions into his heart. When he opened them again, his gaze had returned to its usual calmness and depth. 'The Heavenly Dao Will intends to use Chen Nian to restart the world...' he murmured to himself. 'So the Holy Sect took her away to activate the lock key within her body.' He quickly organized all the clues. 'But did Father pass me the Tianji Record to stop all this? Or...' He paused, a more terrifying thought surfacing.

Mo Xiansheng seemed to have thought of something as well. After a long silence, he spoke: 'Young Master, your father's testament was forcibly severed, which means a higher-level power is intervening. This matter... is likely far more complicated than we imagined.' Chen Ji let out a cold laugh: 'Complicated? I'd like to see just how grand this chess game is.' He tucked the Jade Pendant back into his chest, and in his eyes burned a fighting spirit and killing intent he had never possessed before.

Outside the window, the night wind suddenly rose, causing the candle flame to flicker precariously. Chen Ji stood before the table, his gaze falling on the map that had returned to silence. The runes left by his father, Chen Xuan's figure, the severed testament... all the clues pointed in the same direction—the Heavenly Dao's Eye. He had never been so clear-mindedly aware that between himself and that ultimate existence, there must be a settlement of life and death without end.

Just then, the pages of the Tianji Record flipped again. Chen Ji lowered his head to see lines of ancient seal script slowly appearing on the third page that had always been blank. He had never seen these characters before, yet he understood their meaning the moment he saw them—they were the core secrets of the 'Heavenly Fate Lock Key,' the true meaning of Chen Nian's existence. His pupils contracted violently, and his heart skipped a beat. Mo Xiansheng's voice rang out, carrying irrepressible shock: 'This is... a new guidance! The Tianji Record has manifested on its own!'

dialogue.content: Hold on. Let me first see... what it wants to tell me.

text.content: Chen Ji's voice was unusually calm, like the deathly stillness before a storm. He took a deep breath and focused his gaze on the newly emerged ancient seal script, beginning to identify each character word by word. The candle flame danced in his eyes, reflecting a bottomless darkness. When he finished reading the meaning of those words, his entire body froze—the guidance was not one of salvation, but a cruel truth: once the Heavenly Fate Lock Key was activated, Chen Nian's consciousness would completely dissipate, becoming fuel for the Heavenly Dao Will to restart the world. Unless...

Unless someone was willing to trade their life for another, using the Tianji Record master's Heavenly Fate to substitute the Lock Key and endure the backlash of the Heavenly Dao Will. Chen Ji stared at that condition, finding itutterly ironic. When Father chose to pass down the Tianji Record all those years ago, was it for this very day? He had schemed for over twenty years, arranging every chess piece perfectly, so that one day he could replace Chen Nian and become the one sacrificed? The endgame of this chess game was actually—Father dying in place of son.

Mo Xiansheng seemed to have understood the meaning of those words as well. After a long silence, he spoke with difficulty: 'Young Master... this is your father's layout. He sealed his final wisp of residual soul into the Tianji Record, waiting for your growth. When you had the ability to battle the Heavenly Dao Will, he would reveal this truth to you.' Chen Ji said nothing, only staring fixedly at that line of ancient seal script, his knuckles white from gripping. In the flickering candlelight, his shadow cast on the wall was twisted and lonely.

After a long while, Chen Ji spoke. His voice was very light, as if afraid to shatter something fragile: 'So... from the very beginning, I had no choice.' Mo Xiansheng wanted to say something, but was stopped by Chen Ji's raised hand. His expression had changed—it was a complex look mixing desolation, anger, and resolve. But quickly, that vulnerability was replaced by an even deeper coldness. He was the master of the Tianji Record, the ever-calculating Chen Ji—he would never accept any predetermined fate.

choice.prompt: The text on the third page of the Tianji Record still glowed faintly, seemingly waiting for his response.

choices.description: He, Chen Ji, never believed in fate—if Heavenly Secrets can be changed, then destiny must also be reversible. Even if the cost is to overturn the countless heavens and worlds.
choices.visible_reward: Obtain the opportunity to defy fate

text.content: Chen Ji suddenly laughed. That laughter was light, cold, echoing in the silent chamber, carrying a kind of近乎maniacal的意味. 'Father dying in place of son?' His voice carried mockery. 'Father has underestimated me too much.' He raised his hand to press on the pages of the Tianji Record, spiritual energy surging from his fingertips. 'I, Chen Ji, have schemed across the world for so many years, not to one day send myself into a deadly trap. The Heavenly Dao Will wants to play chess? Then I'll overturn this chessboard!'

The Tianji Record shook violently, the ancient seal script on its pages flickering uncertainly, as if responding to his will. Mo Xiansheng's voice carried astonishment and... a hint of hidden hope: 'Young Master, what do you intend to do?' Chen Ji gave no answer, only casting his gaze toward the heavy night outside the window. In his eyes burned cold flames—that was the most frenzied counterattack that erupts when one is driven to the brink.

choices.description: Father's chess game is not necessarily the only solution—he will carve a bloody path through the deadly trap, finding a method that saves both Chen Nian and himself.

text.content: Chen Ji closed his eyes, forcing himself to calm down. He was the number one waste in Tianqing Sect, a chess player who left nothing to chance—he would never allow himself to be trapped in an either-or dilemma. "Mo Xiansheng," he spoke, his voice regaining its usual composure, "Is this all the information Father left behind?" Mo Xiansheng fell silent for a moment: "That wisp of residual soul has completely dissipated... But Young Master, perhaps there is another way."

dialogue.content: The Tianji Record contains nine pages, but only three have been unsealed. The remaining six pages might hold the key to reversing fate. Mo Xiansheng's voice dropped low: "Young Master, the road ahead is long, but not without hope." Chen Ji opened his eyes, hope rekindling in his gaze. He closed the Tianji Record and murmured softly: "Then... step by step."

choices.memory_label: 决定寻找解封天机录之法

text.content: Night deepened, and the candle finally burned down to its last stub. Chen Ji did not relight it, simply sitting in the darkness as those heavy truths settled in his heart. Father, sister, the will of the Heavenly Dao, the chess game of fate—all intertwined, pressing down on his shoulders. He remembered his mother holding his hand when he was young, saying: "Ji'er, you were born different from others." He hadn't understood then, but now he did. His difference was not some talent, but—the destiny of being chosen.

But this Chen Ji never believed in destiny. Night wind poured through the window crack, stirring his scattered hair. He slowly stood up, tucking the Tianji Record back into his chest. When his palm touched the cool jade pendant, his gaze softened for an instant—that was the last keepsake his father left him, and also the first chess piece for his counterattack against fate. "Chen Nian..." he murmured, "Wait for me. This time, it's my turn to protect you."

Just then, the third page of the Tianji Record suddenly glowed with a ghostly light, and a line of ancient seal script that had never appeared before slowly emerged—it was the core secret about the 'Heavenly Fate Lock Key'.
